answer: An agent exchange for cedar boats serving ocean ports checks the pulse of demand without letting sellers flood its listings. It mails a single-use code to each seller address and pools all accounts at that verified, normalized address under one listing quota. Re-enrollment preserves usage, so aliases at one mailbox gain no extra capacity. Acquiring more premises raises the cost of a swarm, though rented mailboxes can evade this partial defense and housemates must share the quota.
